stories.title: Countries step up aid for Nepal flood disaster
stories.summary: Countries including South Korea, India, China, the UK and the EU are ramping up rescue efforts and humanitarian aid after the devastating Nepal-China floods, with hundreds of foreign nationals still missing. Relief operations remain difficult in the Himalayan terrain, while authorities warn that a lake formed by the disaster could burst and trigger a second wave of flooding.

stories.title: Malaysia’s former human resources minister Saravanan claims trial on graft charges
stories.summary: The 58-year-old pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out.
article_sentences: Former Malaysian human resources minister M.
Saravanan pleaded not guilty to three graft charges involving over RM1 million linked to foreign worker approvals.
The charges include receiving cash and cheque payments as kickbacks for approving 1,000 foreign worker quotas for TYKB Engineering.
Saravanan was granted bail of RM450,000 with conditions, including quarterly reporting to MACC and a ban on harassing witnesses; the case is set for mention on Sept 29.
Saravanan has claimed trial at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to three charges of graft involving more than RM1 million (S$315,800) linked to foreign workers approval.
The 58-year-old pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi here on Aug 28.
“I understand the charges.
I plead not guilty,” said Saravanan.

According to the first and second charges, Saravanan allegedly received RM150,000 and RM350,000 in cash from Vectica Resources director Tan Teck Lim through one Syed Amirul Syed Ahmad at the Bukit Jalil Golf & Country Resorts, and at Jalan Telawi 3, Bangsar on June 16, 2022 and July 7, 2022.
For the third charge, Saravanan allegedly received RM597,000 through a cheque from the same person that was deposited into Big.
Seven Ventures bank account at Maybank Jalan Klang Lama, Taman Desa, on July 7, 2022.
The money was said to be a kickback for him in his capacity as the human resources minister to approve 1,000 quota for foreign workers for TYKB Engineering.

stories.title: Russia’s mass-produced Kuryer combat robot can be controlled via smartphone
stories.summary: The robot is equipped with AGS-17 grenade launchers and 12.7-mm PKT and NSVT machine guns
article_sentences: NOVOSIBIRSK, August 28.

The Kuryer (Courier), Russia’s most widely deployed combat robot in the special military operation zone, is capable of firing weapons, laying and clearing mines, and evacuating the wounded - the platform, which an operator can control with a standard smartphone, was unveiled at the Technoprom forum, a TASS correspondent reports.
The ground robotic system was developed at the Kaps manufacturing company in collaboration with specialists from the Omsk Armored Engineering Institute (OABII).
The Kuryer has a range of more than 10 km and is controlled via fiber-optic cable, cellular communication, or a radio channel.
The robot is equipped with AGS-17 grenade launchers and 12.7-mm PKT and NSVT machine guns.
It is capable of covertly laying mines on a road, carrying out diversionary maneuvers, and firing to destroy targets.
"The robot lays mines on a road in the evening while no one can see it, and by the morning, the enemy will already be driving along it.
In addition to this turret, we can mount completely different add-on modules here.

It could be a smoke-generating system, or it could be a laser device for mine clearance," Vyacheslav Kalabin, a cadet at the OABII, a corporal, and a member of the All-Russian Society of Inventors and Innovators (VOIR), told TASS.
The vehicle is also equipped with a thermal imager and 360-degree cameras, and can deploy TM-62 anti-tank mines.
"This is the most combat-ready and most widely used robot to date," Nurzhan Rakimzhanov, a representative of the Omsk branch of VOIR, told TASS.
The developers did not specify the exact number of systems deployed on the front line, but noted their widespread use in the combat zone.
